Fall Protection Plan

FALL PROTECTION GUIDELINES

MINIMAL FALL PROTECTION SYSTEMS TO BE USED ON THIS JOB

Installation of roof trusses/rafters, exterior wall erection, roof sheathing, floor sheathing and joint/truss activities will be conducted by employees who are specifically trained to do this type of work and are trained to recognize the fall hazards. The nature of such work normally exposes an employee to a fall hazard for a short period of time. This guideline details how Builder’s Bloc will minimize these hazards.

CONTROLLED ACESS ZONES

When using this guideline to implement the fall protection options available, workers must be protected through limited access to high hazard locations. Before any non-conventional fall protection systems are used as part of the work plan, a controlled access zone (CAZ) shall be clearly defined by the competent person as an area where a recognized hazard exists. The demarcation of the CAZ shall be communicated by the competent person in a recognized manner, either through signs, wires, ropes, chains or high visibility paint.

INSTALLATION OF FLOOR JOISTS AND SHEATHING

During the installation of floor sheathing/joists (leading edge construction), the following steps shall be taken to protect workers.

  • AT NO TIME ARE WORKERS ALLOWED TO WALK STEEL BEAMS OR TOP PLATES OF EXTERIOR WALLS without fall protection.
  • Materials for the operations shall be conveniently staged to allow for easy access to workers.
  • The first floor joists or trusses will be rolled into position and secured either from the ground, ladders, or sawhorse scaffolds.
  • Each successive floor joist or truss will be rolled into place and secured from a platform created from additional floor joist that have been laid flat on top of bearing walls.
  • Any workers not assisting in the leading edge construction (e.g. cutting the decking for the installers) shall not be permitted within six feet of the leading edge under construction.
  • Once floor sheathing operations begin, any worker within 6 feet of leading edge construction over 6 feet tall at perimeter of building or stair hole shall use harness and lanyard fall protection or install guard rails first.
  • STAIR HOLES TO BE COVERED OR SURROUNDED BY GUARD RAILS AT ALL TIMES.
  • STAIRS AND BALCONIES TO BE PROTECTED BY GUARD RAILS AT ALL TIMES.

ERECTION OF EXTERIOR WALLS

ERECTION OF EXTERIOR WALLS MUST OCCUR FIRST ONCE THE SUBFLOOR AT ANY LEVEL IS COMPLETE PRIOR TO PERFORMING ANY OTHER TASK!

During the construction of exterior walls, employees shall take the following steps to protect Themselves:

  • A painted line six feet from the perimeter will be clearly marked prior to any wall erection activities to warn of the approaching unprotected edge.
  • Materials for operations shall be conveniently staged to minimize fall hazards.
  • Workers constructing exterior walls shall complete as much cutting of materials and other preparations as possible away from the edge of the deck.
  • All windows to be installed while before wall is raised, or blocked off with 2 rails before raising
  • Workers working in CAZ zone shall be protected by using a harness and retractable device or by erecting a guardrail prior to constructing exterior walls.

INSTALLATION PROCEDURES FOR ROOF TRUSS AND RAFTER ERECTION

During the erection and bracing of roof trusses/rafters, conventional fall protection may present a greater hazard to workers, infeasibility due to truss manufacturer instructions, or swing distance issues that render PFA’s useless. The foreman/competent person shall review the truss manufacturer’s installation documents to determine if trusses are suitable for use as anchor points. Most truss manufacturers do not endorse using trusses as a tie off point while trusses are being set – please review. Please review BCSI bracing details to determine if the bracing would present a greater hazard. The site supervisor should also be aware of swing distances when using PFA systems and recognized truss collapse hazards to determine if using PFA systems during truss setting creates greater hazards than working without PFA systems from the bottom chords of each truss. If the truss manufacturer does not endorse using trusses as an anchor point and the BCSI bracing diagram presents an issue of infeasibility or a condition of greater hazard by putting employees at risk of greater falls trying to brace trusses and establish and anchor point then the following procedures shall be used:

  • Workers shall have no other duties to perform during truss/rafter erection procedures.
  • All trusses/rafters will be adequately braced before any worker can use the truss/rafter as a support or PFA anchorage.
  • Workers will use ladders, scaffolds, stretch boards to secure trusses at exterior walls provided that their feet remain a minimum of 24 inches below the top plate.
  • As an alternative, when ladders, scaffolds, etc. are not the best practice as determined by the site supervisor in areas such as 2-story great rooms or foyers, workers will remain on the top plate using the previously stabilized truss/rafter as a support and PFA anchorage while other trusses/rafters are being erected. Workers may leave the area of the secured trusses only when it is necessary to secure another truss/rafter. Workers will be tied off using Personal Fall Arrest system to a point deemed suitable by the competent person if this method is used. THIS METHOD MUST BE DOCUMENTED ON YOUR SITE SPECIFIC PLAN.
  • The first two trusses/rafters will be set from ladders leaning on the side walls at points where the walls can support the weight of the ladder; and a worker will climb onto the interior top plate via a ladder (3 rungs above plate) to secure the peaks of the first two trusses/rafters being set.
  • Once truss or rafter installation begins, workers not involved in that activity shall not stand or walk below or adjacent to the roof opening or exterior walls in any area where they could be struck by falling objects.
  • Workers working from an interior position using the bottom chords of a truss as a work surface shall have no other duties than securing/bracing the trusses.
  • Workers positioned in the webs of trusses shall work from a stable position by positioning themselves in previously stabilized trusses/rafters and leaning into and reaching through trusses/rafters to gain control of trusses being handled by the crane.
  • With a two part truss, workers positioned at the peaks or on top of the ridge beam shall work from a stable position, either by sitting on a “ridge seat” or other equivalent surface that provides additional stability or by positioning themselves in previously stabilized trusses/rafters and leaning into and reaching through trusses/rafters. Workers using a “ridge seat” for piggy back truss situations must use a personal fall arrest system once trusses have been stabilized. Workers should use a self-looping system and move the tie off point as trusses are set and stabilized to keep anchor points near their position when this situation occurs. Workers should consider setting and sheeting the main trusses and set the cap trusses and corresponding sheeting after main trusses are set and fully sheeted.
  • Workers shall not remain on or in the peak/ridge any longer than necessary to safely complete the task.
  • Once roof trusses have all been set and secured an anchor point should be established for any further roofing operations. Builder’s Bloc recommends installing the first row of sheeting on the front and back of the home first.
  • Workers installing gutter boards must use a personal fall arrest system. Working on the top plates of any exterior wall is prohibited without the use of a personal fall arrest system.

ROOF SHEATHING OPERATIONS

Workers typically install roof sheathing after all trusses/rafters and any permanent truss bracing is in place. Roof structures may be unstable until sheathing is installed. Workers installing roof sheathing may not be able to be protected from all fall hazards by conventional fall protection systems until it is determined that the roofing system can be used as an anchorage point. All workers will ensure that they have secure footing before they attempt to walk on the sheathing, including cleaning shoes/boots of mud or other slip hazards. To minimize the time workers must be exposed to a fall hazard, materials will be staged to allow for the quickest installation of

sheathing.

Workers shall take the following steps to protect workers who are exposed to fall hazards while installing roof sheathing once roof trusses have been braced and stabilized:

  • Once roof sheathing installation begins, workers not involved in that activity shall not stand or walk below or adjacent to the roof opening or exterior walls in any area where they could be struck by falling objects.
  • The competent person shall determine the limits of this area, which shall be clearly communicated to workers prior to placement of the first piece of roof sheathing.
  • The competent person may order work on the roof suspended for brief periods as necessary to allow other workers to pass through such areas when this would not create a greater hazard.
  • The bottom row of roof sheathing may be installed by workers standing in truss webs once they have established a tie off point and are using a Personal Fall Arrest system.
  • After the bottom row of roof sheathing is installed, a slide guard extending the width of the roof shall be securely attached to the roof. Slide guards are to be constructed of no less than nominal 4” height capable of limiting the uncontrolled slide of workers. Workers should install the slide guard while standing in truss webs and leaning over sheathing. This will provide secondary fall protection for workers.
  • All workers conducting roof sheathing operations installed should be tied off using a personal fall arrest system.
  • Additional rows of roof sheathing may be installed by workers positioned on previously installed rows of sheathing. A slide guard can be used to assist workers in retaining their footing during successive sheathing operations.
  • For roofs with pitches between 4-12 and 8-12 slide guards will be placed at 13 foot intervals. Pitches in excess of 9-in-12, slide guards will be installed at four foot intervals.
  • PLEASE STAY TIED-OFF
  • The opening in the roof where material is passed through must have a CAZ line around it and a slide guard just above the opening.
  • When wet weather (rain, snow, sleet, or wind) are present, roof sheathing operations shall be suspended until better weather.

ENFORCEMENT

Constant awareness of and respect for fall hazards, and compliance with all safety rules are considered conditions of employment. The crew supervisor or foreman, as well as individuals in the Safety and Personnel Department, reserve the right to issue disciplinary warnings to employees, up to and including termination, for failure to follow the guidelines of this program.

I have read and reviewed the minimum standard guidelines for fall protection as required by Builder’s Bloc Contracting.
